name: Fess Crag
description: Fess Crag is a small, tidally locked rocky body where one hemisphere bakes in permanent daylight and the other freezes in eternal night. A mountain range runs along the terminator line like a spine, its peaks catching the perpetual sideways light in dramatic chiaroscuro. The sunlit face is a barren expanse of heat-cracked stone, while the dark face is a frozen waste where temperatures plunge deep enough to solidify atmospheric gases if any existed.

The terminator mountains offer the only habitable zone, where temperatures moderate between the extremes and solar power is constant. The silence of an airless world is absolute here, broken only by vibrations transmitted through the rock from thermal expansion and contraction. Walking the terminator ridge offers a view unique in human experience: perpetual golden sunset to one side, infinite starlit darkness to the other, with the mountain's shadow stretching endlessly across the frozen face.

An escape pod debris field scattered across the dark-side foothills tells the story of a vessel that broke apart during an uncontrolled descent. The pods are of civilian design, approximately fifty years old, and show signs of hasty evacuation. Recovery teams found no survivors and no remains, though several pods appear to have been opened from the outside after landing. No record of any ship loss in this system matches the pods' manufacture date or registration codes.

Fess Crag's helium-3 deposits in the regolith make it a potential fuel harvesting site, and the terminator ridge's constant solar exposure is ideal for energy-intensive operations. The mystery of the escape pods draws occasional investigators, but the harsh conditions and remote location have prevented thorough forensic examination. The pods opened from outside present the most troubling question: on a world with no atmosphere and no life, what opened them, and where did the occupants go?
